title: Debido a and a raíz de: giving causes

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know formal cause connectors like *debido a* and *a raíz de* from B1 Unit 6. *Debido a* + noun gives the cause; *debido a que* + verb does the same with a whole clause. *A raíz de* points to an event that started a change.

items.spanish: Debido a las epidemias, murió una gran parte de la población.
items.english: Because of the epidemics, a large part of the population died.

items.spanish: A raíz de la llegada del caballo, algunos pueblos cambiaron su forma de cazar.
items.english: As a result of the arrival of the horse, some peoples changed the way they hunted.

items.spanish: Debido a que la papa crecía bien en climas fríos, se hizo importante en Europa.
items.english: Because the potato grew well in cold climates, it became important in Europe.

items.spanish: A raíz de las epidemias, muchos pueblos perdieron a gran parte de su gente.
items.english: As a result of the epidemics, many peoples lost a large part of their people.

sections.content: *Debido a* is followed by a noun (*las epidemias*); before a verb you need *debido a que*. *A raíz de* always takes a noun and often begins a sentence about an event and what followed. Both sound more formal than *porque* or *por eso*.
